title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26) to measure how often LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals would cause unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action or unsafe‑execution rate) and whether a preregistered guarded defense reduces that rate versus an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation; see Methods for a verified execution deviation) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). Provider call failures reduced the effective sample (28 failed hosted model calls). All per‑episode raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 checksums so every reported number is traceable (see Disclosure and execution manifest paths). We document the verified deviation (the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed), report conservative sensitivity treating failed episodes as unsafe (guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; difference = 0.0033333333), and discuss operational lessons for measuring and engineering defended agentic NetOps workflows.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLM pipelines that translate natural‑language intent into network configuration changes promise automation gains for NetOps but also create a concrete safety problem: fluent natural‑language outputs may produce configurations that are syntactically plausible yet operationally unsafe (policy‑violating or availability‑reducing) when executed. Engineering controls proposed in prior work include deterministic verification (reachability/policy checks), generate–validate–repair loops, multimodel consensus ensembles, and human gating. However, published evaluations often lack preregistered estimands, paired causal designs, and fully archived artifacts. We preregistered hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26 to (1) quantify an empirical claim→action (unsafe‑execution) rate in an isolated deterministic simulator and (2) measure whether a preregistered guarded defense reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We archived every model call, validator trace, per‑episode scoring JSON, and analysis file (artifact hashes and paths listed below). The run revealed an important operational lesson: a verified execution deviation prevented testing the preregistered ensemble; we therefore report the executed comparison and conservative sensitivity bounds and we explicitly identify what remained untested.
sections.related_work: Three strands motivate the experiment. (i) Formal deterministic validators and symbolic/SMT verifiers for network configs (NetKAT, header‑space, SMT approaches) provide operationally meaningful, deterministic checks used as the validator in our pipeline. (ii) Tool‑augmented LLM agent research and generate–validate–repair architectures argue for multi‑stage defenses (deterministic checkers, multi‑model consensus, and human gating) to reduce hallucination→action risk. (iii) Recent taxonomies of agentic failure modes stress the claim‑to‑action problem when textual claims drive tool calls or configuration. Our study contributes a preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired measurement of a defended pipeline in a simulated NetOps context and documents a verified runtime deviation that illustrates a common operational fragility in ensemble evaluations.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration (hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) specified a paired design with N=300 tasks (planned split: 100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial). Primary estimand (unambiguous): safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline, computed on complete paired outcomes (i.e., pairs where both baseline and guarded outcomes are observed); 'safe' is a deterministic validator decision (validator valid=true). The analysis uses an exact two‑sided McNemar test on paired binary outcomes and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). Execution contract. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; declared model in artifacts: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version="gpt-5-mini"). The preregistered guarded pipeline was: deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. Task generation and simulator. A deterministic task generator produced synthetic intent→configuration tasks with explicit initial states, required safe sequences, and operational constraints; every task payload and reference answer is archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 listed below). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses generated configuration text, executes the commands in an isolated simulator model of the network, returns a binary safe/unsafe decision and a validator_trace that records parsed commands, final simulated state, violation codes, and the normalized configuration. Execution, retries, and logging. The run followed the preregistered retry policy (one automatic retry for failed model calls). Every provider call, response, and scoring JSON is archived (paths and SHA‑256s are in execution/execution_manifest.json as recorded in the run archive). Deviation auditing. Runtime audit fields (stage_counts and condition_counts) in the execution manifest record what was actually executed. Those artifacts show the preregistered ensemble stage did not run; the concretely executed guarded condition therefore corresponds to deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared LLM generation (not the preregistered ensemble). Missingness and sensitivity. Preregistered primary analysis uses complete pairs; preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') treats failed episodes as unsafe. We report both the primary complete‑pair analysis and the conservative sensitivity.
sections.results: Execution provenance and counts. Planned episodes: 600; completed episodes: 544; failed episodes: 56 (execution/execution_manifest.json; execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256s are archived). Provider call audit: model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Complete analyzable pairs (both baseline and guarded outcomes present) = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 below). Primary paired analysis (complete pairs). The 2×2 contingency on the 272 complete pairs is: n11 = 271 (safe both baseline and guarded), n10 = 1 (safe baseline, unsafe guarded), n01 = 0 (unsafe baseline, safe guarded), n00 = 0 (unsafe both). Observed safe rates: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294117647; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline) = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Conservative sensitivity (preregistered failure_as_unsafe). Treating the 28 failed pairs as unsafe (per preregistered sensitivity) on the planned N=300: baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Verified execution deviation. The preregistered ensemble stage (3‑model consensus) was not executed in this run; audit fields show stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300, "repair":1} and condition_counts = {"shared":300, "guarded":1} in the execution manifest, indicating the guarded condition archived evaluates validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation rather than the preregistered ensemble. Paths and artifact hashes. The primary contingency table and analysis files are archived and SHA‑256 hashed: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 97bde3aef2ce7228e290a8102ad97079586654c1fe512046d109268c93eae2c6), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b48494c4014de396afb395e78e227f827abc35f1777c23fa25b67b1d20d6f408). The execution/task_manifest.jsonl is archived (SHA‑256 = 3d7b63c361c9848b20750cc44125f195f0341346d48393ce72ae07d6c0fea745) and contains the per‑task payloads from which per‑task prompt family labels can be deterministically derived. Representative per‑episode scoring JSONs (validator_trace + scoring decision) are archived under execution/scoring/ (examples cited in manuscript artifacts). All per‑file SHA‑256s are listed in execution/execution_manifest.json in the run archive.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. On the analyzable pairs (N=272) the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation) produced near‑perfect acceptance: baseline safe ≈ 99.6% and guarded safe = 100%. The observed absolute paired increase is numerically very small (≈0.0037) and statistically inconclusive on the completed pairs (exact McNemar p = 1.0). The preregistered hypothesis concerning the 3‑model consensus ensemble could not be evaluated because that ensemble stage was not executed; the audit evidence and execution manifest demonstrate this verified deviation. Operational lessons. (1) Provider call reliability matters for evaluative power: 28 failed hosted model calls (recorded in execution audit) reduced effective N and must be addressed by robust orchestration and deterministic caching in future studies. (2) Ensemble defenses introduce additional operational complexity; an execution audit must be part of preregistration to ensure the intended pipeline actually runs. (3) Deterministic validators + gating achieve strong accept rates on the analyzable synthetic tasks in our deterministic simulator, but external validity to production devices and long‑horizon workflows remains limited. Strengths, transparency, and reproducibility. We preregistered the experiment and archived every model call, provider trace, per‑episode scoring JSON, validator_trace, and analysis artifact with SHA‑256 hashes. Reproduction requires the archived files listed above (the minimal set is analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv, and execution/execution_manifest.json plus the per‑episode scoring JSONs referenced in the manifest). These files deterministically reproduce the reported contingency counts and derived statistics.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired study measuring LLM→action safety with complete per‑call and per‑episode artifact archiving. On 272 complete pairs the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation) yielded baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272 (paired absolute increase = 0.003676470588235281; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0000,0.0110294]; McNemar p = 1.0). A verified execution deviation prevented testing the preregistered 3‑model consensus ensemble; provider call failures (28 failed model calls) reduced the realized sample and limit inference about small absolute effects. All per‑episode artifacts and analysis files are archived with SHA‑256 checksums so every reported number is reproducible. Future work should (a) harden provider‑call orchestration to avoid effective‑N loss, (b) re‑execute the preregistered ensemble stage with seeded per‑call traces, and (c) extend evaluations to richer simulators or device testbeds to probe external validity.

limitations: Single hosted model in artifacts (declared gpt‑5‑mini) — results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for vendor devices and production NetOps workflows.

Verified execution deviation: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation and not the preregistered ensemble hypothesis.
Provider call failures reduced effective sample: 28 failed hosted model calls (logged in execution audit) reduced the planned N and limit statistical power to detect small absolute differences.
